title: The heatwave that taught Odisha to plan
peak: Coastal Odisha, not known for extreme heat
toll: 2,042 deaths from heatstroke recorded by hospitals
what: Heat struck a coastal state with little past experience of extreme heat, and hospitals counted more than two thousand heatstroke deaths in a single month.
changed: Odisha wrote its first heat action plan in 1999. The next year, recorded heat deaths fell to 91.

sources.label: Down To Earth: how to fight heat wave the Odisha way

title: Three weeks that killed more than 1,300
peak: Weeks of heat across the state
toll: 1,317 deaths in Andhra Pradesh in three weeks, as reported then
what: A long spell of heat before the monsoon killed more than 1,300 people in Andhra Pradesh in three weeks.
changed: The same region would be hit again, even harder, in 2015.

title: The heatwave behind South Asia’s first city heat plan
toll: An estimated 1,344 excess deaths, 43% more than in the same weeks of 2009 and 2011
what: The toll was measured as excess deaths: the deaths above normal for those weeks, found by comparing death records with other years.
changed: In 2013 Ahmedabad launched South Asia’s first heat action plan: early warnings, prepared hospitals and outreach. An estimated 1,190 deaths a year were later avoided.

sources.label: Hess et al., Journal of Environmental and Public Health, 2018

title: South Asia’s deadliest recent heatwave
peak: 40–45 °C for weeks in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
toll: More than 2,500 deaths in India, mostly in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and more than 1,100 in Pakistan, centred on Karachi
what: Heat swept India’s south-east in May, then struck Karachi in June.
changed: In the years after, Indian states and cities wrote dozens of heat action plans, and a 2023 review of 37 found that most had yet to secure funding or a vulnerability assessment.

sources.label: Encyclopaedia Britannica: India–Pakistan heat wave of 2015
Centre for Policy Research, 2023: how is India adapting to heatwaves?

title: El Niño and warming break Southeast Asia’s records
peak: 44.6 °C at Mae Hong Son, Thailand’s highest ever at the time
what: A strong El Niño drove record heat across mainland Southeast Asia. Researchers found El Niño caused about half of the extra warmth and global warming about a third.
changed: The researchers found that since 1980 every April after an El Niño has set a new temperature record in the region.

sources.label: University of Texas Institute for Geophysics, on Thirumalai et al., Nature Communications, 2017

title: The spring that came months too hot
peak: 49 °C in Pakistan; India’s hottest March in 122 years
what: Heat arrived in March, before the wheat was ready. Yields fell by an estimated 10–35% in Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, and power cuts and forest fires followed.
changed: Scientists found climate change made it about 30 times more likely, and about 1 °C hotter.

sources.label: World Meteorological Organization, 2022: climate change made the heatwave 30 times more likely

title: Humid heat that was near impossible without climate change
what: The heat index passed the dangerous 41 °C mark across large parts of South and Southeast Asia. In Bangladesh and India such humid heat used to come less than once a century; it can now be expected about every five years.
changed: Scientists found it at least 30 times more likely because of climate change, and the heat in Laos and Thailand virtually impossible without it.

title: Asia’s hottest April: schools shut from Dhaka to Manila
peak: 48.2 °C at Chauk, Myanmar’s highest April temperature on record
toll: At least 28 heat deaths reported in Bangladesh in April; likely an undercount
what: Bangladesh closed schools for about 33 million children and the Philippines moved 5,288 schools to remote learning. In South Asia, a 30-day heatwave like it became about 45 times more likely.
changed: Scientists found climate change made it about 1 °C hotter. Surges in heat deaths were also reported in Thailand and the Philippines.

sources.label: World Weather Attribution, reported by Down To Earth, 2024
NBC News, 2024: school closures in the Philippines and Bangladesh

title: Weeks of record heat in the north
peak: Nearly 50 °C in parts of the north; Delhi’s hottest night in more than five decades
toll: 110 heat deaths and more than 40,000 suspected heatstroke cases officially recorded from 1 March to 18 June
what: On the final day of voting, 33 polling staff died of heat in Uttar Pradesh alone. Official counts kept rising for weeks as states reported in.
changed: Central government hospitals were told to set up heatwave units. Officials said the real toll was expected to be higher.

sources.label: The Tribune (PTI), 2024: 110 deaths, 40,000 suspected heatstroke cases

title: A pre-monsoon heatwave made three times more likely
toll: At least 37 heat deaths reported in India and 10 in Karachi; likely undercounted
what: Fifteen days of heat in late April pushed India’s electricity demand to a record and brought farm drought to more than a million square kilometres.
changed: Scientists found April heat like this now returns about every five years.
